description_en: Bhīmabhakteśvara Mandira was constructed by Prime Minister Bhīmasena Thāpā and his wife Bhaktakumārī in 1823 CE (VS 1879). Although the name literally means ‘Bhīma-the devotee of Śiva’, it appears the temple was named after its donors Bhīmasena Thāpā and Bhaktakumārī.Standing next to Kṛṣṇa Temple (KAT0710) south of the Lũhiti, the golden spout at Sundhārā in Kathmandu, the dome-styled temple has an influence of the Mughal style as well. With a gilded finial on top, the temple has aśivaliṅgaestablished inside the sanctum as the main deity.Thāpā constructed the temple at the Janaralabāga (lit. general’s garden). He also endowed lands to form aguṭhīfor performing daily and other periodic rituals at the temple, along with feeding mendicants on various occasions and brahmins on the occasion of Bhīmasena Thāpā’s birthday. The longest-serving head of ministers between 1806-1837 CE, Bhīmasena Thāpā introduced an entirely new form of temple that he named Bhīmabhakteśvara Mandira. Its plan followed conventional patterns with a square sanctum and an inner ambulatory. The core emerged from the base to support a bulgy dome (Gutschow2011, p.874). More temples in foreign style were built after the construction of Bhīmabhakteśvara (Tiwari2013, p.175). About a year after its construction, Bhīmasena Thāpā’s younger brother Raṇavīrasiṃha Thāpā offered a bell at the temple. In 1865 CE (VS 1922), the second wife of Bhīmasena Thāpā endowed 77ropanīs of land from various parts of Nepal for theguṭhīto perform various rituals at the temple.A foundation formed in the name of Bhīmasena Thāpā is currently (November 2022) looking after the temple besides managing the performance of daily and periodic rituals. The descendants of Māthavarasiṃha Thāpā perform daily rituals here at the temple. The anniversary ritual (varṣavarddhana) of the temple is performed every year on the day of Śivarātrī, the 14th of the dark fortnight of Phālguna.
description_ne: यो मन्दिर विसं १८७९ (सन् १८२३) मा प्रधानमन्त्री जनरल भीमसेन थापाले धर्मपत्नी भक्तकुमारीको साथमा स्थापना गरेका थिए ।सुन्धारामा रहेको धरहरादेखि दक्षिणतर्फ रहेको कृष्ण मन्दिर (KAT0710) सँगै भीमभक्तेश्वर मन्दिर रहेको छ । गुम्बज शैलीको यस मन्दिरमा मुगल कलाकृतिको प्रभाव देखिन्छ । मन्दिरमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यो मन्दिर विसं १८७९ (सन् १८२३) मा प्रधानमन्त्री जनरल भीमसेन थापाले धर्मपत्नी भक्तकुमारीको साथमा आफूले बनाएको जनरलबाग (बागदरवार) मा आफ्नै नामले मन्दिर स्थापना गरेका थिए । भीमसेन थापाले भक्तिपूर्वक स्थापना गरेको शिवमन्दिर हुनाले यस मन्दिरलाई उनकै नामबाट भीमभक्तेश्वर भनिएको हो । उनले मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजा लगायत सन्यासीहरूलाई भोजन खुवाउन, भजनमा सहभागीहरूलाई पारिश्रमिक दिन, दुईवटा ठूला एकादशीहरूमा पूजा गर्न, श्रावण महिनामा भीमसेन थापाको जन्मदिनमा देवता पूजा गरी ब्राह्मणहरूलाई भोज खुवाउन, शिवरात्रीमा पूजा गर्न विभिन्न ठाउँहरूमा खेत गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । यसै मन्दिरको निर्माणपछि नेपालमा विदेशी शैलीका मन्दिरहरू निर्माण गर्ने क्रम शुरु भएको थियो (Tiwari2013, p.175) । विसं १८८० (सन् १८२४) मा भीमसेन थापाका भाइ रणवीरसिंह थापाले भीमभक्तेश्वर मन्दिरमा घण्टा चढाएका थिए । विसं १९२२ (सन् १८६५) मा राजा राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाहको राज्यकालमा भीमसेन थापाकी माहिली श्रीमतीले भीमभक्तेश्वर मन्दिरको लागि नेपालका विभिन्न ठाउँहरूमा ७७ रोपनी जग्गा गुठी राखिदिएकी थिइन् । विसं २०५६-२०५७ (सन् १९९९-२०००) मा  राष्ट्रिय विभूति भीमसेन थापा स्मृति प्रतिष्ठानको सहभागितामा पुरातत्त्व विभागबाट मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।अहिले (सन् २०२२ नोभेम्बर) यस मन्दिरको रेखदेखको जिम्मेवारी राष्ट्रिय विभूति भीमसेन थापा स्मृति प्रतिष्ठानले लिएको छ । मन्दिरको सुरक्षा र पूजाआजाको व्यवस्थापन त्यसै संस्थाले गर्दै आइरहेको छ । अहिले माथवरसिंह थापाका सन्तानले मन्दिरको नित्यपूजा गर्दै आइरहेको छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष शिवरात्रीको दिनमा मन्दिरको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गरिन्छ ।
brick_type: dāci apā (conical veneer brick), mā apā (regular fired brick)
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number KAT0700_I_001 Sources N. Yogī VS 2010, pp.14-17 The inscription that documents the establishment of the temple on the second day of March in 1823 was removed from its original place and found broken into three pieces in front of the temple. It is currently (2022) leaning against the northern boundary wall. The inscription was read by Nutan Sharma in 1983 and translated by Mahesh Raj Pant in collaboration with Bishnu Raj Jha and Nutan Sharma. Of the entire 41 lines, the first nine lines are in Sanskrit, the following ten in Nepālī ( deśabhāṣa ). The final 22 lines give 85 place names of fields in Kathmandu, Bhaktapur and Thimi with a total income of 932 muri (ca. 7.85 ha of agricultural land). Details H: 160 cm, W: 98 cm Translation: “O Bhīma. Why do you afflict the mind resembling the lake Mānasarovāra. The mind is ever haunted by the fear accompanying existence. The full moon-like feet of Bhīmabhakteśvara are ever-shining. Among the five brothers [ sodareṣu – of the same uterus] to whom Satyarūpā – in the wake of the stability and prosperity ensured by the king of Gorkhā – the devoted [ sati ] wife of minister [ saciva ] Amarasiṃha, son of Vīrabhadra, gave birth to General Śrī Bhīmasena, the head of the ministers [ mantriśiromaṇi ], who is successful [ kṛtī ] in achieving noble deeds. In the year 1879 of Śrīvikrāma, when the sun is in Aquarius, in the month of Caitra, in the dark fortnight, on the day of Brahmā, a Monday, he and his wife Bhaktakumārī, who is a good devotee [ bhakti ] built a wonderful temple [ mandira ] near Kāntipura, in his own auspicious garden [ janarala bāg ] and consecrated formally Śrī Bhīmbhakteśvara, together with ornaments, a flower garden beautified by a pond. He dedicated two villages [ grama ] in addition to nine fields [ kṣetra ]. Let the person respecting the rules connected with this place obtain endless merit [ puṇya ]. So that all may be understood, the particulars are written in the local language [ deśabhāṣa ]: After building the temple with ornaments and other items, janaral Bhīmasena Thāpā installed the image of Bhīmabhakteśvara Mahādeva in his own garden near Kāntipura. He set apart tax free land [ suvā ] for the performance of daily [ nimitty ] and seasonal [ naimittika ] worship of the image. Free distribution of food (should be provided) daily to (mendicants such as) jogis and sannyāsis as well as phakīras , salaries [ ṣānagī ] and expenses [ ṣarca ] be paid to the officiating priest [ pūjāhāri ], the temple attendant [ ṭahaluva ], the singers [ bhajana garnyā, bājā bajāūnyā ] for the morning and evening performances, the sweeper [ baḍhārnyā ] as well as the members of the association [ guṭhī ] in Śālivāhanaśake saṃvat 1744, according to Vikramāditya Saṃvat 1879 on Wednesday the 17th  of the month of Phāguṇa, on the second day of the dark moon of the month of Caitra. An association [ guṭhī ] has been established with a total income of 932 muri of rice (ca. 8.5 tons) for the perpetual worship [ pūjā ] and offering of cooked rice [ bhoga ], for the distribution of 15 portions [ bhāg ] of alms, the performance of offering water to the liṅga [ jaladhārā ] in the months of Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha (mid April to mid July), for the worship (of Viṣṇu) on the occasion of the two Great Elevenths [ thulā ekādaṣī ] (in July and November), for the Devatāpūjā and the feeding of the Brahmins [ brāhmaṇabhojana ] on the birthday of the general in the month of Śrāvaṇa, for the worship and great bath [ mahāsnāna ] on the day of Haritālikā (on the 3rd  day of the bright half of the moon in Bhādra), for worship on the day of the dark night of Śiva (Śivarātrī, the 14th  day of the dark half of the moon in the month of Phāguṇa), for the donation of husked rice, salt and other food items [ sidhā ] and kitchen utensils [ sarajāma ] to devotees and pilgrims on the anniversary of the temple and its deity [ varṣavaṃndhana ], the worship on the day of Śrīpañcamī (the 5th  day of the bright half of the moon in the month of Māgha/January), for altogether 25 caretakers of the association [ guṭhiyār ] – that is the head of the association, the clerk, two persons in charge of distributing alms, two attendants of the deity ([ devatā kā ṭahaluvā ], one Brāhmaṇa as priest, one Brāhmaṇa as attendant, one Brāhmaṇa who prepares the cooked rice for the deity, seven singers [ bhajanyā ], seven Kusle musicians [ bājā vajāunyā kusalā ], one sweeper [ baḍhārnyā kusalyā ], one head of the tillers [ mohināyeka ]”.

historical_events.event_description: Prime Minister Bhīmasena Thāpā, together with his wife Bhaktakumārī, constructed the temple at the Janaralabāga (lit. general’s garden). He also endowed lands to form aguṭhīfor performing daily and other periodic rituals at the temple, along with feeding mendicants on various occasions and brahmins on the occasion of Bhīmasena Thāpā’s birthday.
Raṇavīrasiṃha Thāpā (text: Raṇabila), younger brother of Bhīmasena Thāpā, offered a bell at the temple.

The second wife of Bhīmasena Thāpā endowed 77ropanīs of land from various parts of Nepal for theguṭhīto perform various rituals at the temple. The inscription instructs the concerned persons to keep track of the expenses for the rituals and enter the remainder into the deity’s treasury.
The Bhīmasena Thāpā Foundation and the Department of Archaeology collectively renovated the temple.

The old priest house of theBhīmabhakteśvara Guṭhīwas renovated and the office of the Nepal Hotel Byawasayi Samaj, an organization of hotel entrepreneurs, was set up here with the assistance from the Sundhārā Āmā Samuha, a group of elderly ladies from Sundhārā area.
